posts.text:
Jason seems to have two different personalities in GTA 6, and I think that people calling him boring could do with rewatching Trailer 2. 

During the montage at the start of Trailer 2 we see him entirely in his comfort zone. His day-to-day cycle consists of fixing up his house (which he doesn’t pay for), extorting businesses for Brian, working out, and buying beer. He’s completely familiar with this way of living, there’s nothing particularly that stressful or unbeknownst to him about this routine. 

I think this explains why in the very first sequence of the trailer he’s witty with Brian in a way that we haven’t really seen much else of the time. “What, that’s why you came by?” and then sarcastically reciting “Love you, Jason” under his breath. 

This sense of familiarity and comfort ALL changes as soon as Lucia gets out of prison and the both of them get into the mess that kicks off the main story. Their “easy score” goes wrong and all of a sudden Jason is in completely uncharted territory. As a result of this, his guard goes up, and his more serious (potentially military-like) persona that we’ve seen in a lot of newer material comes into play. 

We still get some of his dry sarcasm in the Extended Look, but only when he’s 1-on-1 with Lucia, probably because this is where he feels the most comfortable. “Yeah, you’re the perfect criminal.” (referencing her getting locked up), and “Miss me?” etc etc. 

Basically, I think that Jason’s arc will likely resolve around him opening up and becoming more adjusted to their circumstances over the course of the main story. We know that Jason and Lucia have different ambitions from their character bios, Lucia wants to go right to the very top of the criminal world, whereas Jason is much more conservative about his goals. Jason becoming more closed off after they’re thrusted into trouble as opposed to Lucia’s continued goofiness is meant to represent this difference between them.
